claim: The first sale came from a YouTube build posted for fun, not from a freelancer pitch.
reasoning: The client could see a similar thing already working; email was in the description.
mechanism: Publish build → email in description → inbound email → calls → scope → yes.
evidence: “the client found me on YouTube because I had built something similar on my channel just for fun, and he emailed me.”
conditions: Public demo that matches the buyer’s want; reachable email; he will hop on calls and scope.
exceptions: No inbound if there is no similar public artifact, or no email, or he refuses paid work framing so hard that he never scopes.
action: Ship the build in public with a reachable address; wait for “I want something similar.”
confidence: high as his origin story; survivorship (we hear the one that emailed).
speaker: Nate Herk

claim: The close was “scoped the build / I could do it / he said yes.” Not a proposal deck in this clip.
reasoning: Buyer already wanted the similar thing; remaining work is fit + confidence.
mechanism: Couple of calls → scope → verbal yes.
evidence: “We hopped on a couple of calls. I scoped out the build. I told him I could do it. He said yes. It was that simple.”
exceptions: Cold outbound will not be “that simple.”
action: On inbound-similar, spend the calls on scope, not on “I am a freelancer.”
confidence: high for this deal; low as a general close rate.
speaker: Nate Herk
